chunks: From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Hafs, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

The diyyah of the Saluqi dog is forty dirhams; the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم assigned that for it. The diyyah of the sheep dog is a ram, the diyyah of the farm dog is a jarib of wheat, and the diyyah of the house dog is a qafiz of dust for its owner.

key_terms.جَرِيبٌ: a measured quantity of land produce or grain assessment used here as compensation
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a unit of silver currency used here to state compensation
key_terms.دِيَةُ: legal compensation due for killing or injuring property or life in this context
key_terms.قَفِيزٌ: a known measure used here in stating compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah for different kinds of dogs in Shi'i hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal compensation values for different categories of dogs based on their recognized use and benefit. It attributes the ruling on the Saluqi dog to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and distinguishes between hunting, herding, agricultural, and domestic dogs in determining liability.
